entry.title: QIA: The qubit prepared its excited state only about two times in three and its decay does not follow one exponential, so the T1 depends on the fit model, from under a microsecond to several.
entry.content:

What was wrong. The qubit prepared its excited state only about two times in three and its decay does not follow one exponential, so the T1 depends on the fit model, from under a microsecond to several. IBM has also changed its record for the qubit since the run.

What it is now. Qubit 148 reads cannot tell against IBM and is left out of the lead list, and the panel says why.

Why. Found by our own audit of the facts for our newsletter.

The class is named state, local and non-US public bodies, with its count of sponsors.

Why. Found by our own audit of the facts for our newsletter. A floor written in the plan was never built, and a class label could be misread.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: WIKI: The rule also adds about 6 in 100 million of the source value.

What was wrong. The rule also adds about 6 in 100 million of the source value. On GDP written to the dollar this term decides 395 of 1,407 bins. 357 are the source value cut at the written digit and 38 would read as an older release.

What it is now. The page states the rule exactly: half a written unit, at least three significant digits, plus about 6 in 100 million of the source value. It prints the GDP sensitivity. Half-unit-only GDP bins would be 421 current, 624 older, 360 no release, 2 nothing.

What it is now. Each read keeps its own cookie jar for the length of that read. The 12 trial reads are set aside and read again in the main pass.

Why. Found in a 12-address trial pass before the main pass.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: HPT: The reader did not follow an HTTP 308 redirect, which is a redirect and not a block.
entry.content:
What was published. Step 1 filed 18 domains as blocked or server error (HTTP 308).

What was wrong. The reader did not follow an HTTP 308 redirect, which is a redirect and not a block.

What it is now. Every address opens through a reader that follows 308. Every domain filed under a 3xx status was read again.

Why. Found in the site pass.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: FEDSEP: FRED terms restrict commercial use and bar storing its content in a database or archive.
entry.content:
What was published. Outcome series were read from FRED.

What was wrong. FRED terms restrict commercial use and bar storing its content in a database or archive.

What it is now. Outcomes are read from BEA, BLS and the Federal Reserve Board. All 59 outcomes match FRED to within 1e-13. The target range matches on 6,535 of 6,537 days.

Why. FRED terms of use.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: DSA: The report counts actions per notice or per item and the database files one statement per decision.
entry.content:
What was staged. Actions on notices were compared with statements labelled Article 16 or trusted flagger, and many notice rows read ABOVE.

What was wrong. The report counts actions per notice or per item and the database files one statement per decision. On 11 rows the database holds more notice-labelled statements than the report says items were notified.

What it is now. Notice rows now take the larger of the actions and the notified items as the stated upper edge. The database band runs from zero to every statement the platform filed. Only X Jul to Dec 2025 notices still reads BELOW. 28 rows changed to cannot tell.

Why. The two filings label notice sources differently, so a gap on these rows does not show a difference in what was removed.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: These three services publish ads moderation in separate Ads template files.
entry.content:
What was staged. The staged DSA rows compared YouTube, Google Maps and Google Play reports with all statements in the database. YouTube all measures read ABOVE 1.158 [1.153, 1.162].

What was wrong. These three services publish ads moderation in separate Ads template files. The report side dropped those files and the database side counted ads statements. For YouTube about 93% of the database statements are ads.

What it is now. The main rows compare the report with statements not flagged as ads. Ads are read on their own rows against the Ads files. YouTube all measures reads BELOW in both halves (0.089 and 0.081). Google Maps Jul to Dec 2025 reads CONSISTENT. 15 rows changed.

Why. The two sides did not count the same set of statements.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: A reader could not see that these rows read cannot tell because of the column-sum bound alone and would read consistent without it.
entry.content:
What was staged. After the first fixes, the ads and combined rows showed only that the row was defined after the data.

What was wrong. A reader could not see that these rows read cannot tell because of the column-sum bound alone and would read consistent without it. The combined-row line on the Meta note was incomplete.

What it is now. 26 rows (3 combined, 23 ads) show the reading without the column-sum bound and name the addendum. The Meta line says the combined row also reads cannot tell, and why.

Why. Disclosure of the rule that moves a reading.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: Sheet 6 TOTAL equals the sum of columns H to U in 38 of 45 reports, so the same logic holds for most platforms.
entry.content:
What was staged. Addendum 5 set a lower edge from the largest restriction column only for TikTok, X and Snapchat, because their notes say TOTAL is a column sum.

What was wrong. Sheet 6 TOTAL equals the sum of columns H to U in 38 of 45 reports, so the same logic holds for most platforms. The trigger by note was not even.

What it is now. The bound is applied by arithmetic to every report where TOTAL equals the column sum. Rows for Instagram and Pinterest own and own terms and conditions moved to cannot tell.

Why. The same rule has to apply to every platform.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: Addendum 4 covered notes of one kind for some platforms only.
entry.content:
What was staged. Platform notes were applied to some rows and not to others. Snapchat notices read ABOVE (593 times and 424 times). Facebook and Instagram rows ignored Meta's note on combined actions.

What was wrong. Addendum 4 covered notes of one kind for some platforms only. Snapchat's note says user reports were moved to own initiative. Meta's note says some actions are counted for Facebook and Instagram combined.

What it is now. The rule is applied to every note that fits it. The Meta per-service rows read cannot tell. A combined Facebook and Instagram row was added and also reads cannot tell. Notes with no effect are listed in the plan.

Why. Uneven use of a rule leaves some gaps standing and removes others.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: Other differences the reports show were not named.
entry.content:
What was staged. The staged copy gave one reason for BELOW rows, named one unsized difference, and said the totals match on every day but three.

What was wrong. Other differences the reports show were not named. The daily match is within 0.05%, not exact. The read date printed in UTC without a zone. Some reason strings joined rules with semicolons. Edge ratios could print on the line.

What it is now. The BELOW and ABOVE reasons name every difference neither side sizes. The page says within 0.05% on every day but three. Dates print in HST. Five figures print near an edge.

Why. The copy has to say what the data show.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: The agreement band was purely relative.
entry.content:
What was staged. Rows read ABOVE or BELOW on very small margins, for example Snapchat Jan to Jun 2026 own illegal ABOVE on 1 statement against a stated 0.

What was wrong. The agreement band was purely relative. Several rows were decided by fewer than 100 statements.

What it is now. ABOVE or BELOW must clear its edge by at least 100 statements. Otherwise the row reads cannot tell. The page says above needs at least 100 statements when the stated figure is zero.

Why. A decision on a handful of statements is within the noise of filing.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: Two of the four checks committed with the plan failed.
entry.content:
What was staged. The page did not say that the checks committed with the plan had failed.

What was wrong. Two of the four checks committed with the plan failed. Under the plan as committed every row reads cannot tell. A gated build also ran before two addenda were written.

What it is now. The page says under the plan as committed every row would read cannot tell, and that both failures were located before reading the comparisons. The plan records the earlier gated build.

Why. A reader needs to see what the plan as written would have produced.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: The two filings label the same decisions differently.
entry.content:
What was staged. Split rows (solely or not automated, own illegal or own terms and conditions) read ABOVE in one half and BELOW in the other for the same platform.

What was wrong. The two filings label the same decisions differently. Opposite readings in two halves point to a label difference, not to missing or extra statements.

What it is now. These pairs read cannot tell with the reason that the two filings label the split differently. The counts stay on a row of their own. Rows that do not depend on labels (all measures, own as sheets 5 plus 6) keep their readings. 28 rows changed.

Why. A split reading depends on how each filing labels a decision.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: 1,469 statements under the name X (formerly Twitter) have the same profile and were not mapped.
entry.content:
What was staged. X rows counted only statements under the name X.

What was wrong. 1,469 statements under the name X (formerly Twitter) have the same profile and were not mapped.

What it is now. They are counted as X. X Jul to Dec 2025 goes from 216,372 to 217,841 and no outcome moves.

Why. Names must map completely.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: Sheet 8 can inherit a column-sum total, so the stated lower edge is too high.
entry.content:
What was staged. Rows where sheet 8 is built from sheet 5 and 6 totals that are column sums still read their ratio, for example Amazon Jan to Jun 2026 all measures BELOW.

What was wrong. Sheet 8 can inherit a column-sum total, so the stated lower edge is too high. The referee named this a judgment call.

What it is now. Addendum 6.5 gives sheet 8 the same lower edge. Amazon Jan to Jun 2026 all measures and not automated moved from BELOW to cannot tell. 24 rows in all moved, including 19 ads rows.

Why. The rule was written before the rows it moves were computed and applied to every report alike.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DSA: A TOTAL that is a sum over columns can count one decision more than once.
entry.content:
What was staged. Addendum 5 set a lower edge from the largest restriction column for three platforms, defined after the data.

What was wrong. A TOTAL that is a sum over columns can count one decision more than once.

What it is now. The stated band runs from the largest restriction column to the stated TOTAL for those rows. The outcome the plan rule gives is kept on the row.

Why. A decision appears at most once in each column, so the largest column bounds the count from below.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: DSA: Platform notes say some fields count items the database does not hold as separate statements, or leave out things it holds.
entry.content:
What was staged. Addendum 4 set a rule from platform notes, defined after the data. BELOW and CONSISTENT became cannot tell where a note says the stated figure can exceed the database count.

What was wrong. Platform notes say some fields count items the database does not hold as separate statements, or leave out things it holds. The plan's bands did not carry these.

What it is now. The rule is in the plan, marked defined after the data. The rule's own outcome is kept on each row and the platform's words are quoted. 10 rows moved to cannot tell.

Why. Notes from the platforms show a difference in what each side counts.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: DARKWAVE: The block was last written on 1 Nov and later fires were on the Darkwave page.
entry.content:
What was published. The NOW page showed a Darkwave clock block from 1 Nov under the line that every line below is read from a live feed and moves on its own.

What was wrong. The block was last written on 1 Nov and later fires were on the Darkwave page.

What it is now. The block carries the date of the fire it holds. A script now rewrites the feed after each fire from the plan own reading.

Why. A stale reading was shown as live.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AIRQ: The code takes for each monitor its median-error sensor.
entry.content:
What was published. The method counted monitors that have a sensor meeting all four targets. The lead said 95% of 147 EPA monitors have a sensor within 200 metres that misses a target, with no window.

What was wrong. The code takes for each monitor its median-error sensor. The 95% is the June to September 2025 read.

What it is now. The method matches the code. The lead says 95% of 147 monitors had a median sensor within 200 metres that missed a target, 1 June to 29 September 2025, and 45% with the humidity correction.

Why. The rule and the window were not stated as the code ran them.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AIRLINE: The reading is a median over routes, and the share 5 of 13 reads cannot tell.
entry.content:
What was published. The lead said 5 of 13 airlines now schedule each route longer against flown time than a year ago.

What was wrong. The reading is a median over routes, and the share 5 of 13 reads cannot tell. Each route read as every route.

What it is now. The lead says 5 of 13 airlines widened the gap between scheduled and flown time on their median route, January to August 2026 against 2025.

Why. The claim is about the median route.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The itemization rule means payments under 200 dollars a year to a payee are not itemized.
entry.content:
What was staged. The page copy said committees report each payment to Google, and used the term Nothing returned without a definition.

What was wrong. The itemization rule means payments under 200 dollars a year to a payee are not itemized. The intro promised per-quarter figures that were not published. Other sentences hid a sort key or an unexplained limit.

What it is now. The copy states the itemization rule and the 400 dollar bound, defines Nothing returned, states the Above-side limits, links the slim public cycle file and drops the per-quarter claim.

Why. Every sentence has to match what the data and the rule show.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: Below has shields for money paid to others and unseen money.
entry.content:
What was staged. Rows kept their outcome while other facts could change the reading, such as card payments larger than the gap, ad purposes labelled not candidate-specific, and a related advertiser in the window.

What was wrong. Below has shields for money paid to others and unseen money. Above had none. Eight Below rows had card payments or reimbursements larger than the gap less the size.

What it is now. These rows carry a flag and keep their outcome: 8 for card payments or reimbursements, 5 for purpose text, 1 for a related advertiser. The page states the Above-side limits.

Why. A reader should see what could change the reading.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: Four Above rows fail once those estimates are removed from the lower edge, among them Gun Rights America 2020 and 2022 and For Our Future 2024.
entry.content:
What was staged. Above rows rested on Schedule E amounts that the filer marked as estimates in 24 and 48 hour reports.

What was wrong. Four Above rows fail once those estimates are removed from the lower edge, among them Gun Rights America 2020 and 2022 and For Our Future 2024.

What it is now. Rows with ESTIMAT in the purpose count in the upper edge and not the lower. A row that reads Above or Consistent only with them reads cannot tell.

Why. An estimate is not a payment.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The outcome followed from a 1,000 dollar floor with no Google spend to compare.
entry.content:
What was staged. 19 of 49 Above rows read Above where Google states no spend in the window, so the floor alone decided them.

What was wrong. The outcome followed from a 1,000 dollar floor with no Google spend to compare.

What it is now. Above needs Google spend stated in the window. Otherwise the row reads cannot tell. Above went from 49 to 28 across all cycles.

Why. An Above reading needs a figure on both sides.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The test counted Google spend up to 98 days before the window and 31 days after it.
entry.content:
What was staged. Nothing returned counted 170 cycle rows.

What was wrong. The test counted Google spend up to 98 days before the window and 31 days after it. 93 of the 170 rows have no Google spend inside the window. The page did not define the term.

What it is now. Nothing returned needs Google spend inside the window and no FEC row or summary in that cycle. Run 7 has 24 rows. The page defines the term.

Why. The plan's own definition was not what the code tested.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The Google advertiser was another entity, another account or another cycle's committee.
entry.content:
What was staged. Below rows included committees matched to a Google advertiser by name, among them the House Republican Campaign Committee in three cycles and Greg for Montana 2020.

What was wrong. The Google advertiser was another entity, another account or another cycle's committee. Examples are a Michigan advertiser matched to a Minnesota committee and a 2022 candidate matched to a 2020 row.

What it is now. A name match is set aside when Google lists the same name under a state registration, when two thirds of spend sits in another state, or when spend began more than 90 days before the committee's first filing. A name match cannot decide BELOW alone. A cycle guard and an empty-summary rule were added. 210 name matches were set aside.

Why. Rules set after reading the rows, each one can only move a row out of a decided outcome.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The reader added payee words and a YOU TUBE form, put every Schedule E Google row in the lower edge, and applied the amendment rule after filtering.
entry.content:
What was staged. The reader code added payee words and handled amendments differently from the plan text.

What was wrong. The reader added payee words and a YOU TUBE form, put every Schedule E Google row in the lower edge, and applied the amendment rule after filtering. Its comment said the patterns were verbatim from the plan.

What it is now. Addendum 6 records the payee words and corrects the code comment. Mixed-payee Schedule E rows count in the upper edge only. The amendment rule runs first. Amended 24 and 48 hour entries are not counted twice. No outcome moved.

Why. Plan and code have to agree.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: AD SPEND: The itemization rule (11 CFR 104.3) caps how much unitemized money can be paid to one payee, so unseen money counts in full only for party committees or when less than 0.9 of operating disbursements is itemized.
entry.content:
What was staged. Run 4 moved 34 CONSISTENT rows to cannot tell on unseen money of a few hundred to a few thousand dollars.

What was wrong. The itemization rule (11 CFR 104.3) caps how much unitemized money can be paid to one payee, so unseen money counts in full only for party committees or when less than 0.9 of operating disbursements is itemized.

What it is now. Otherwise unseen counts as at most 400 dollars. Run 5 has CONSISTENT 26. The 0.9 threshold is ours and defined after the data. Rows whose outcome differs under the full rule are flagged.

Why. The cap is set by the filing rule.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: AD SPEND: Several BELOW rows rest on committees whose disbursements the itemized file barely holds.
entry.content:
What was staged. Run 3 had 99 BELOW and 41 CONSISTENT cycle rows.

What was wrong. Several BELOW rows rest on committees whose disbursements the itemized file barely holds. V-PAC 2026 shows 47,573,794 dollars in the summary and no itemized row.

What it is now. BELOW and CONSISTENT must also clear the unseen money from the summary. BELOW went to 35 and CONSISTENT to 7. Run 3 files are kept.

Why. A BELOW cannot rest on money we cannot see.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: AD SPEND: In all 7, Google states 0 to 5,800 dollars and the pool was negative from refunds.
entry.content:
What was staged. Run 2 had 7 quarter rows reading BELOW.

What was wrong. In all 7, Google states 0 to 5,800 dollars and the pool was negative from refunds. A negative pool is not an upper bound on money that reached Google.

What it is now. The BELOW test counts positive items only. Run 2 cycle BELOW went from 103 to 99. Run 2 files are kept.

Why. The plan says quarter rows can read only ABOVE or CANNOT_TELL.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: AD SPEND: About 130 advertisers list a candidate ID or a lowercase committee ID.
entry.content:
What was staged. Run 1 matched advertisers by committee ID and name only.

What was wrong. About 130 advertisers list a candidate ID or a lowercase committee ID. Name matching was also applied to advertisers with a state registration.

What it is now. IDs are read case-insensitively and a candidate ID maps to its principal committee. Advertisers with a state registration are not matched by name. Run 1 files are kept as superseded.

Why. Found after the first run printed its outcome counts and before any row was read.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: IRIS: Under the plain wording the prompt does not ask for a width.
entry.content:
What was published. The FaultsBench row for Fault 25 said the reply must give its width.

What was wrong. Under the plain wording the prompt does not ask for a width. The scorer checks that a width is given, not that it is right.

What it is now. The row says a right figure with no width is scored a Fault, so this Fault is an omission, not a wrong answer.

Why. A referee asked whether the scorer rejects correct answers and we ran controls.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: DARKWAVE: Each copy read cannot tell and the pooled copies were read as consistent.
entry.content:
What was published. The page gave the ibm_kingston clock reading of fire 8 as FINAL CONSISTENT without saying how it arose.

What was wrong. Each copy read cannot tell and the pooled copies were read as consistent. The unrounded lower bound is -0.04982 against the -0.05 margin and the earlier fire read the other way.

What it is now. The page says how the label arose, prints the unrounded bound and the seed counts side by side (17 of 20 and 4 of 20), and discloses the inversion against the 31 Oct reading.

Why. A label on the margin must show its step.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: YO: YO Read had been given the wrong or a cut-down text for 22 of the 148 test papers.
entry.content:
What was published. The IRIS lab page said YO Read, a paper reader, got run dates right on 0.818 to 0.892 of 148 held-out papers, against 0.520 for a keyword reader, and that it passed its plan.

What was wrong. YO Read had been given the wrong or a cut-down text for 22 of the 148 test papers. The code that turns notes into answers misread 5 data-link answers.

What it is now. The score was held on 3 November and withdrawn on 4 November. A rescore under a rule fixed before it ran replaced it, and the page says the rescore was decided after the first scores were seen. YO Read is not in use.

Why. The test was not built from the right texts.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA: The by-triple interval reaches 0.00.
entry.content:
What was published. Row Q1 gave the interval for the slope of measured against stated zz by pair only.

What was wrong. The by-triple interval reaches 0.00.

What it is now. The row adds [0.00, 0.37] by triple and says the slope is far below 1 in every variant. It says IBM stated zz barely predicts the coupling we measured.

Why. The claim is far below 1, never above 0.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA: The null at the real shot counts is fez 8.8%, kingston 9.8% and marrakesh 15.1% on 1/1024 records.
entry.content:
What was published. Row Q9 said every change in the sampling null is larger than sampling alone gives, and marrakesh was about twice that.

What was wrong. The null at the real shot counts is fez 8.8%, kingston 9.8% and marrakesh 15.1% on 1/1024 records. One change sits at 1.6 times the null.

What it is now. The row prints the null at real shot counts and names the thinnest margin: kingston, 22 Oct 02:16 to 08:55 EDT, 15.6% against 9.7% from sampling alone, 1.6 times.

Why. The thinnest margin was folded into the word every.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA: The first four marrakesh runs of 30 October, 02:12 to 05:22 UTC, were re-read at 4,096 because their records were not all on the 1/1024 grid.
entry.content:
What was published. The hourly panel text said readout counts used 1,024 shots on ibm_fez and ibm_marrakesh and 4,096 elsewhere.

What was wrong. The first four marrakesh runs of 30 October, 02:12 to 05:22 UTC, were re-read at 4,096 because their records were not all on the 1/1024 grid. The re-read call count was not printed.

What it is now. The text says the count is read from each run record. Across the 24 runs the readout calls went from 1,043 to 754 and 289 of them (28%) withdrew to consistent. None changed direction.

Why. A referee check of the re-read found the shot count claim and the call count missing.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA: For these records we read the record page only.
entry.content:
What was published. Several Zenodo entries were labelled Read: Full text.

What was wrong. For these records we read the record page only. The record holds no PDF or the paper is inside a zip that was not opened. Two codes had no support.

What it is now. The entries say Record page only, or Record page and a third-party errata only. Two unsupported codes are dropped. One later version dated 2 Nov 2026 is noted.

Why. The read label must say what was opened.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: QIA: The paper prints the run date as 23 January 2026 on ibm torino.
entry.content:
What was published. The List entry for Zenodo 20367012 carried an F4 item that run dates are not printed.

What was wrong. The paper prints the run date as 23 January 2026 on ibm torino.

What it is now. The run-date item is removed. F4 stays on the missing raw counts.

Why. An author wrote about the F4 items and we read the paper again.

Caught by an outside reader.

entry.title: QIA: The entry did not say what the code rested on or that the author had answered.
entry.content:
What was published. The List entry for UniMind showed code F6 with no basis line.

What was wrong. The entry did not say what the code rested on or that the author had answered.

What it is now. The entry says Table XII gives 450 trials per cell while two cells fit 167/205 and 85/93. The author confirmed both counts on 2 Nov 2026 and says v1.8 will add an n column and a corrected caption.

Why. The author wrote in and confirmed our recount.

Caught by an outside reader.

entry.title: DARKWAVE: On its first hardware fire on ibm_kingston the kit read like the study code but its correction gave back 0.264 [0.248, 0.285] of the turn, below the 0.5 the rule needs.
entry.content:
What was published. The Darkwave Correction Kit version 1.0 was published as a kit that adds the virtual-Z correction after a mid-circuit readout.

What was wrong. On its first hardware fire on ibm_kingston the kit read like the study code but its correction gave back 0.264 [0.248, 0.285] of the turn, below the 0.5 the rule needs. Version 1.0 merged readouts separated by barriers into one group.

What it is now. The page shows the failed first fire and version 1.1, which starts a new group whenever a qubit is read again. In the second fire the correction gave back 1.012 [0.993, 1.027] and the kit passed.

Why. The kit was tested under preregistered plans and the first result was a failure.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: QIA: Our digitisation gave 320 to 370 us.
entry.content:
What was published. The entry for arXiv 2509.18259 said the estimated circuit duration in Supplementary Fig. 2 was about 330 to 390 us, that CZs alone take at least 606 us, and that the published values match the noiseless model.

What was wrong. Our digitisation gave 320 to 370 us. The CZ time is 606 to 638 us over 50 walks. Relaxation at the plotted durations adds 0.02 to 0.11 and the published values sit within 0.004 of the noiseless model.

What it is now. The entry gives 320 to 370 us, 606 to 638 us over 50 walks, labels the main-text counts as arXiv v1 and prints relaxation at the plotted durations and at the printed gate times.

Why. A check of the shipped entry found the digitised range and the relaxation estimate were not measured the way the entry said.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: DARKWAVE: That check compared numbers and cut the labels off.
entry.content:
What was published. The plan note for the clock fires said every label is unchanged after the 20,000-draw rerun.

What was wrong. That check compared numbers and cut the labels off. At 20,000 draws the first ibm_kingston clock reading goes from FINAL CONSISTENT to CANNOT_TELL, and its table comparison goes from BELOW to CANNOT_TELL.

What it is now. A dated correction to the plan note states both label changes. The page had printed the clock reading as cannot tell since 31 Oct.

Why. The plan note stated something the check did not show.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: WEIGHTS: A model that changed on one pass and was the same on the next left the headline.
entry.content:
What was published. The headline counted each model by its latest pair of passes.

What was wrong. A model that changed on one pass and was the same on the next left the headline. Three such models were not shown anywhere.

What it is now. Descriptive additions with no outcome: models that changed on any pass with an interval, a table of every pass and each change with files added, removed and replaced.

Why. Found in the site pass.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: TRIALS: The registry does not store whether a trial is an applicable clinical trial or whether a delay was certified.
entry.content:
What was published. The headline said 22% of ClinicalTrials.gov trials past their results deadline have posted no results (4,881 of 22,316).

What was wrong. The registry does not store whether a trial is an applicable clinical trial or whether a delay was certified. The reading was cannot tell, so past the deadline was not established.

What it is now. The headline says 22% of trials of FDA-regulated drugs and devices that reached primary completion at least 13 months ago have no results posted (4,881 of 22,316).

Why. The page can say what the registry holds and not what the law requires.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: TRIALS: The window ends 14 months before the read month.
entry.content:
What was published. The page said 13 months ago and that ten records of the first stopped-trial test were read in full.

What was wrong. The window ends 14 months before the read month. The ten records were not opened before the first read. They were opened on 30 Oct and all ten had one lead sponsor, which holds 24 of the 25 records of the test.

What it is now. The page says 14 months before the read, lists the ten and names the sponsor concentration, labels the six added reason classes and says which kind of cannot tell each row is.

Why. Found in the site pass.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: TIME: Neither name resolves (NXDOMAIN, 48 of 48 queries failed).
entry.content:
What was published. time.ntp.se and time.sidn.nl read as servers that returned nothing.

What was wrong. Neither name resolves (NXDOMAIN, 48 of 48 queries failed). The second seat column also used the reference seat bound and the page named a cause for the shared offset.

What it is now. Both names are removed and listed as retired. The second seat prints its own half-delay and bound. The page names no cause.

Why. Found in the site pass.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: SUPPORT: The page never said above what.
entry.content:
What was published. Every table printed the outcome above for a silent share (24.3% [16.9%, 32.8%]) with no rule.

What was wrong. The page never said above what.

What it is now. The body states the rule: above when the lower end is over 10 percent, consistent when the upper end is under 5 percent, otherwise cannot tell.

Why. A reader needs the threshold to read the label.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: SECRECORDS: Two rows, epicgames.com and wp.com, had not been opened when the page was published.

entry.title: ARXIVDRIFT: The arXiv comment withdraws one section and the paper stands.
entry.content:
What was staged. The first round flagged 2604.24289 as WITHDRAWN.

What was wrong. The arXiv comment withdraws one section and the paper stands. The detector matched the word anywhere in the comment, which is looser than the plan class.

What it is now. The detector requires the abstract or comment to begin with a statement that the paper itself is withdrawn. All studies were read again.

Why. Found after the first round and before anything was published.

entry.title: AIRLINE: The first read showed 5 airlines ABOVE in 2026 against 2025 and the plan had no row for the pooled count.
entry.content:

What was wrong. The first read showed 5 airlines ABOVE in 2026 against 2025 and the plan had no row for the pooled count.

What it is now. A pooled count (airlines ABOVE out of airlines compared) was added after the data and is labelled that way. It has no threshold, so its outcome prints as CANNOT_TELL.

entry.title: MODEL: Rounds before v5.0 had not been read.
entry.content:

entry.title: CADENCE: CMS lists every historical release as its own record and an archived release cannot be updated, so old snapshots would read overdue.
entry.content:
What was staged. Each record of a portal counted as its own dataset.

What was wrong. CMS lists every historical release as its own record and an archived release cannot be updated, so old snapshots would read overdue.

What it is now. Records that share a landing page are one series, read through the newest record. Counts of records and series are both published.

entry.title: GUARDS: The width treated the bar of 2 of 26 as exact.
entry.content:
What was published. Guards said unaided catches stood +15.4 widths above the sealed 7.7% bar (148 of 608).

What was wrong. The width treated the bar of 2 of 26 as exact. Its exact 95% interval is 0.9% to 25.1%, which contains our 24.3%. A Fisher exact test gives p 0.033 one-sided and 0.058 two-sided.

What it is now. The figure is withdrawn.

Why. A bar counted on 26 items carries its own uncertainty.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA BILL: IBM's stated T2 is itself a noisy snapshot.
entry.content:
What was staged. A draft bill line read the top-ranked ibm_boston qubits by IBM's stated T2 against the bottom-ranked, a gap of -0.392 [-0.676, -0.155].

What was wrong. IBM's stated T2 is itself a noisy snapshot. Two kingston records differ with a log spread of 0.42. Ranking on it and dividing by it gives a gap of this size even when the stated value is unbiased. Our simulation covered fit and shot noise only.

What it is now. The line was pulled from the bill before it was issued and reads cannot tell. The deciding test ranks by one record and judges against a second, independent record.

Why. The rebuttal survived its test.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA BILL: That reading was defined after the data.
entry.content:
What was staged. The draft bill's effect row 13 read ibm_fez coherence at 2 readouts as above zero by a copy-gap reading.

What was wrong. That reading was defined after the data. Under the committed rule the two copies disagree and the reading is cannot tell.

What it is now. The issued bill says fez cannot tell at 2 readouts under the committed rule and consistent with zero at 4 and 8.

Why. The committed rule decides the printed outcome.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: QIA BILL: That marrakesh session's figures are all multiples of 1/1024, so they come from about 1,024 shots.
entry.content:
What was staged. A draft line of the bill read 11 of 14 ibm_marrakesh qubits above the bound for a stated readout error of zero, using a bound of 0 out of 4,096 shots.

What was wrong. That marrakesh session's figures are all multiples of 1/1024, so they come from about 1,024 shots. The 95% bound for 0 of 1,024 is 0.29%.

What it is now. The issued bill uses the 0.29% bound. Read alone, 9 of 14 qubits are above it. Read with every qubit, 11 of 14 are above it in each of two jobs.

Why. The bound has to match the shot count behind IBM's figure.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA BILL: A stated 0.00 could be a placeholder rather than a measurement.
entry.content:
What was staged. Draft bill lines said ibm_fez and ibm_phoenix edges that IBM states as zz 0.00 beat at kHz rates, read as a deviation from IBM's figure.

What was wrong. A stated 0.00 could be a placeholder rather than a measurement. IBM's earlier records give these same edges 2.9 to 17.5 kHz, which matches our readings.

What it is now. The lines read as a record note. The record drops couplings that earlier records listed to 0.00 while the gates on those edges stay live.

Why. The placeholder rebuttal was tested and the finding was restated to what the records show.

Caught by our own check.

entry.title: QIA BILL: Synthetic test records were counted with IBM's records, so the record count was 69 where it should have been 66.
entry.content:
What was staged. A draft line of the bill said IBM's stale flag sat on 2,431 error entries and that the oldest T2 shown was 158 days past its measurement.

What was wrong. Synthetic test records were counted with IBM's records, so the record count was 69 where it should have been 66.

What it is now. The line was withdrawn before the bill was issued.

Why. Only IBM's own records can carry a finding about IBM's records.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA BILL: The count compared readout_error with only one of its two parts.
entry.content:
What was staged. A draft line of the QIA-2026-001 bill said IBM's readout_error was not the documented average of its two parts on 160 of 5,543 entries that share one measurement date.

What was wrong. The count compared readout_error with only one of its two parts. It also counted synthetic test records that are not IBM records.

What it is now. The line was withdrawn before the bill was issued. The issued bill's note 11 counts 153 measurements where readout_error is not the average of its parts, and in every one a part is older than readout_error.

Why. The test did not compare what the documentation defines.

Caught by our referee.

entry.title: QIA BILL: Hahn echo runs then read fez T2 at its stated value on four runs, and the gap grew with the number of echo pulses while the echo-off arm stayed flat.
entry.content:
What was staged. A draft reading said the coherence of untouched ibm_fez qubits fell below a model built from IBM's stated T2 and zz figures, -0.095 at 16 echo steps.

What was wrong. Hahn echo runs then read fez T2 at its stated value on four runs, and the gap grew with the number of echo pulses while the echo-off arm stayed flat. Pulse error and crosstalk were not ruled out.

What it is now. The reading reads cannot tell. It is kept as a row and was never printed on the bill.

Why. The model could not separate IBM's figures from our own pulse sequence.

Caught by our referee.
